title: Air India, Singapore Airlines Drop Codeshare Booking Rule on 126 Weekly Flights
excerpt: From October 15, travellers can book eligible Air India or Singapore Airlines flights between India and Singapore on a standalone basis through either carrier's channels, ending the requirement to pair codeshare legs from both airlines.
body:
• From October 15, Air India and Singapore Airlines will sell eligible India–Singapore codeshare flights on a standalone basis, ending the rule that forced travellers to combine a flight from each airline in a single booking.
  • The change covers 126 weekly flights between Singapore and eight Indian cities: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kochi, Kolkata and Mumbai.
  • Bookings can be made through either carrier's website, mobile app or appointed travel agents — an SIA-operated flight can be bought alone on airindia.com, and an Air India-operated flight on singaporeair.com.
  • From the second quarter of 2027, top-tier Maharaja Club and KrisFlyer members get reciprocal priority check-in and boarding, while Silver-tier members get extra baggage allowance and priority boarding on eligible routes.

Air India and Singapore Airlines will allow customers to book India–Singapore flights on a standalone basis from October 15, ending a longstanding restriction that forced travellers to pair a codeshare flight operated by one airline with a flight operated by the other. The change is the first phase of the Commercial Cooperation Framework Agreement the two carriers signed in January this year, and it covers 126 weekly flights between Singapore and eight Indian cities.

Under the existing arrangement, an eligible Air India-operated codeshare flight booked through SIA must include an SIA-operated flight, and the mirror requirement applies in reverse. From October 15, that requirement falls away: customers can book eligible flights operated by either airline on a standalone basis through the other carrier's website, mobile app and appointed travel agencies.

Context & Background

The bundle-only rule was a legacy of how the codeshare was originally structured. Codeshares let airlines sell seats on each other's flights, but the Air India–SIA version came with a catch: book through one carrier and you had to include a leg flown by the other. Travellers comparing fares or building simple point-to-point itineraries often ended up adding segments they did not need, or abandoning the codeshare and booking direct with the operating airline.

The two airlines have been steadily deepening their commercial ties. In April, they expanded reciprocal mileage earning so Maharaja Club and KrisFlyer members can earn miles on a wider range of flights operated by either airline. Singapore Airlines holds a 25.1 per cent stake in Air India, and the pair currently codeshare on 77 destinations across 27 countries, connecting through hubs in Delhi, Mumbai and Singapore to points across Asia, Europe, North America and Australia.

Impact & Analysis

The immediate effect is simpler shopping. A traveller who prefers Singapore Airlines' schedule on the Singapore–Delhi sector can now buy that seat through Air India's channels as a standalone ticket — useful when Air India is running a fare sale or when the traveller wants everything on one Maharaja Club account. The reverse works too. With 126 weekly flights across the eight cities on offer through both booking channels, travellers get a wider range of itinerary and timing combinations without the old bundling constraint.

"By building on the strengths of our two airlines, we aim to bring greater consistency to the travel experience of our common customers between India and Singapore, whilst delivering greater choice, convenience and value,"

— Nipun Agarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Diaspora Angle

The India–Singapore corridor is one of the busiest for the Indian diaspora — professionals, students and families shuttle constantly between the city-state and home. The standalone-booking rule is a practical win: festive-season trips, student travel and visiting-family itineraries can now be booked as single tickets on whichever carrier has the better schedule or fare, without padding the itinerary with an unwanted extra leg.

One clarification: this codeshare change is separate from Air India's own network moves. A different October 7 announcement had Air India shifting its mainline international flying out of Chennai to its low-cost arm Air India Express. The codeshare change applies to bookings across both carriers' flights — including Chennai, which remains one of the eight cities covered.

What's Next

The second wave of benefits lands in the second quarter of 2027, when elite frequent flyers get reciprocal perks on eligible routes: Maharaja Club Platinum and KrisFlyer PPS Club members gain priority check-in and boarding, while Silver-tier members receive extra baggage allowance and priority boarding. The airlines are also working on improved schedule connectivity to cut layover times, corporate offerings and further phases of the framework agreement — all aimed at making the combined network behave more like a single airline for the customer.
